citations.quote: The safety of KYGEVVI was evaluated in a prospective, open-label, single-arm study in pediatric and adult patients with genetically confirmed TK2d previously treated with pyrimidine nucleosides (Trial 1). Additional safety information was derived from retrospective chart review studies (Study 1, Study 2) and from an expanded access program [see Clinical Studies (14)].

The efficacy of KYGEVVI for the treatment of patients with TK2d, with an age of symptom onset on or before 12 years of age, was established based on data from one Phase 2 clinical study (Trial 1), two retrospective chart review studies (Study 1, Study 2), and an expanded access program.
Trial 1 (NCT03845712) is a prospective, open-label, single-arm study in 47 patients with genetically confirmed TK2d previously treated with pyrimidine nucleosides.
Study 1 (NCT03701568) was a retrospective chart review study in 38 patients with genetically confirmed TK2d treated with pyrimidine nucleosides.
Study 2 (NCT05017818) was a retrospective chart review study in 61 patients with genetically confirmed TK2d (43 untreated patients and 18 patients treated with pyrimidine nucleoside therapy).

population.text: Adult and pediatric patients with genetically confirmed thymidine kinase 2 deficiency (TK2d) with age of symptom onset ≤12 years, previously treated with pyrimidine nucleosides.

citations.quote: A total of 82 patients with genetically confirmed TK2d and the age of symptom onset \le 12 years were treated with KYGEVVI or pyrimidine nucleosides. Efficacy was assessed by comparing overall survival in the treated patients to an external control group of untreated patients matched to treated patients using age of TK2d symptom onset (\le 2 years or > 2 to \le 12 years). A total of 78 matched pairs were identified.

endpoint.text: Overall survival (survival compared to matched untreated external control) — the primary efficacy endpoint.

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint is overall survival (OS) time. Per the SAP, time to death is calculated from both age of TK2d symptom onset and age of treatment initiation. This review primarily focuses on time from treatment initiation to death as recommended by the Agency.

target_moa.text: KYGEVVI is a combination of two pyrimidine nucleosides (doxecitine and doxribtimine) that provides a balanced increase in deoxycytidine and deoxythymidine, bypassing the impaired TK2 salvage pathway; incorporation into mitochondrial DNA increases mtDNA copy number to restore mtDNA synthesis in TK2 deficiency.

citations.quote: Doxecitine and doxribtine are both pyrimidine nucleosides. The proposed mechanism of action of this two-drug combination is the balanced increase of substrate levels of both deoxynucleosides: doxecitine and doxribtine, bypassing the impaired TK2 salvage pathway pyrimidine nucleotide synthesis in TK2d. The incorporation of the exogenous doxecitine and doxribtine into mtDNA leads to increased mtDNA

TK2d is a rare autosomal recessive mitochondrial disease that results in deficient activity of thymidine kinase 2 (TK2). Deficiency of TK2 results in a shortage of phosphorylated pyrimidine nucleosides within the mitochondria leading to mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) depletion and deletions. key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5%) are diarrhea, abdominal pain, vomiting, and increased ALT and AST. In treated patients (N=47): diarrhea 72% (34), abdominal pain 23% (11), vomiting 21% (10), ALT increased 21% (10), AST increased 17% (8). Dose reductions occurred in 22% and permanent discontinuation in 9% of patients.

summary.text: KYGEVVI was approved via a traditional (not accelerated) approval under a 505(b)(2) NDA with priority review in the Division of Rare Diseases and Medical Genetics. The product had orphan drug designation for TK2d, and the sponsor was granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher. Effectiveness was based on an external-control survival comparison supported by mechanistic confirmatory evidence.
